C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS.Name: Bounded, serialized forward-update path: deadlines on check and download, one install at a time, idempotent rollback-snapshot reuse, fresh-data install toasts, and honest backup-channel evidence
C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS.Summary: The forward update path check→download→install is unbounded and unserialized at every layer: neither the renderer nor m016 passes any timeout (the plugin documents "When it is not set, the requests do not time out" — tauri-plugin-updater 2.14.1 src/updater.rs:328-329), so a stalled gateway or mirror wedges the check or the ~14-31 MB package download forever with no visible refusal; installSignedUpdate (src/renderer/src/commands/index.js:1305-1353) has no in-flight guard, so the two independent entries (file.check-update and the notice's INSTALL_UPDATE) can run concurrent installs that race two mt_rollback_prepare snapshot copies of the ~30 MB bundle; every prepare wipes staging.tmp and re-copies even when an intact snapshot of the running version is already staged; and the install toasts are built from the hours-old check snapshot queued in the notice (status.latestVersion), not from the fresh plugin re-check the flow itself performs. This change bounds every network hop of the forward path with named constants passed through the plugin's own timeout seams (CheckOptions.timeout and downloadAndInstall options, plus UpdaterBuilder::timeout in m016), makes a timed-out hop a visible localized failure (never a silent "no updates"), serializes installs with a renderer single-flight guard, makes a repeated prepare reuse an intact staging set instead of re-copying it, derives the user-visible toasts from the fresh re-check, and pins — with zero external network — that the backup feed channel (GitHub latest.json mirror) delivers the package itself through the URL its feed carries, under the deadline. The package URL staying gateway-only is recorded as the owner's deliberate C-UPDATER-STATS decision, not relitigated.

Problem.Description: (1) No deadline anywhere on the forward path. tauri.conf.json plugins.updater (:79-88) carries only endpoints/pubkey/installMode — no timeout; mt_updater_check awaits updater.check().await bare (src-tauri/src/m016_updater.rs:76), and the plugin's UpdaterBuilder::timeout is never called; the renderer's installSignedUpdate calls check() and update.downloadAndInstall() with no options (src/renderer/src/commands/index.js:1333-1334, 1340), although the installed plugin (package.json ^2.14.1, installed 2.14.1) exposes CheckOptions.timeout ("Timeout in milliseconds", dist-js/index.d.ts:17) and DownloadOptions.timeout (:36) that both plumb straight into the Rust request builder (2.14.1 src/commands.rs:56-57, 182-184; applied as the reqwest whole-request timeout at src/updater.rs:591-593 and :849-851). A hung response therefore wedges the 24 h launch check silently and forever (RUN_LAUNCH_CHECK awaits invoke('mt_updater_check') — src/renderer/src/store/autoUpdates.js:279 never settles), and a wedged install leaves the user in "Updating to Mark X…" indefinitely with no failure state. The contrast inside the same zone: the rollback transport got exactly this discipline in C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC (ROLLBACK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS=10, ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS=300, ROLLBACK_RESTORE_DEADLINE_SECS=660, src-tauri/src/m068_rollback.rs:125-133, pinned by tests at :2892-2927); the forward path was flagged read-only there (its F-004) and remains untouched. (2) No serialization and no idempotent prepare. installSignedUpdate has no in-flight guard; the notice button merely hides the card (autoUpdates.js:346-359) and file.check-update is an independent second entry (:1355-1380) — two overlapping invocations each run mt_rollback_prepare (commands/index.js:1324), whose command body is spawn_blocking(prepare_inner) with no lock and no already-staged check (m068_rollback.rs:2407-2412), and prepare_inner unconditionally removes staging.tmp and re-copies the ~30 MB bundle (:466-472, the macOS copy at :498-508). The deferred predecessor states it plainly: "F-008 stays cut: prepare_inner and installSignedUpdate untouched" (m068_rollback.rs:66-67) — this change is the remediation group that discharges that cut. (3) Stale snapshot reaches the GUI. INSTALL_UPDATE hands the notice's stored check snapshot to installSignedUpdate (autoUpdates.js:302, :347-355), which builds its visible toasts from it — `Updating to Mark ${status.latestVersion}…` (commands/index.js:1337) and `Mark ${status.currentVersion} is up to date` (:1345) — while the actual install runs on the fresh plugin re-check (:1334); the code's own comment bounds today's honesty to "a stale status can only mislabel a toast, never install the wrong build" (:1309-1310). A user clicking a notice queued hours earlier sees the wrong target version in the progress toast when the feed moved. (4) The backup feed channel does not provide a backup package channel, and nothing demonstrates that it even delivers the package. Both latest.json composers write platform urls through the counting gateway — release.yml:697/:853/:1174/:1206, "https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/pkg/{platform}/${VER}" — a deliberate C-UPDATER-STATS decision ("the latest.json platform url fields route through the counting gateway … every URL still resolves to the same GitHub bytes", release.yml:32-36), and DownloadOptions carries no alternative URL. So when the gateway is down, the package is unfetchable even while both feed endpoints answer; that residue is owner-owned (see NonGoals). What this change can and must pin honestly: the plugin's endpoint failover (2.14.1 src/updater.rs:545-658 — per-endpoint continue on any failure including non-deserializable bodies, success breaks) fetches latest.json from the second, GitHub-mirror endpoint and then downloads the package through the URL that mirror's feed carries, under the caller's deadline — the Wave-4 criterion "for the backup channel, verify obtaining the package itself" (criterion of 2026-11-22, translated from Russian) — and no test anywhere exercises this today; the repo's only injectable network seams are m068's Fetch trait (m068_rollback.rs:1208-1222) and the e2e tauri shim (tests/e2e/update-notice.spec.ts:61-123, tests/e2e/fixtures/tauri-shim.ts:205-239 which intercepts plugin:updater|* invokes too).

C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS.Relationship: Zone lineage, all read as predecessors: C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK (#120) introduced mt_rollback_prepare and wired it fail-closed into installSignedUpdate before downloadAndInstall — this change keeps that ordering binding and only makes a repeated prepare idempotent against an intact staging set; C-UPDATER-STATS (#165) deliberately made the gateway the sole carrier of package URLs (its R-3) — this change records the single-package-URL consequence as that owner decision and pins the feed-carried-URL-plus-deadline contract instead of adding an alternative URL; C-WIN-ROLLBACK-PANIC gave the rollback transport its deadlines (10/300/660 s, m068_rollback.rs:125-133) and explicitly cut F-008 ("prepare_inner and installSignedUpdate untouched", :66-67) with F-004 (forward-path deadlines) assigned to "the separate updater remediation group" — this bundle is that group and discharges the F-008 cut (single-flight), the scout's UPDATER-INSTALL-REPREP and UPDATER-STALE-CHECK-DATA keys together, while the F-003/F-005 residues (source failover, an independent GitHub package download) stay recorded owner decisions, not silently absorbed, bringing the same bounded-wait discipline to the forward path; C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY is the honesty precedent this change follows for failure states — a bounded failure settles into a distinct, localized error state, never masquerades as an ordinary empty result ("no updates"), and raw error text stays console-only. Source: WAVE4 scout 2026-11-22 (main bb68fd6c), bundle "Бандл A — UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS", keys UPDATER-NO-DEADLINE, UPDATER-BACKUP-SAME-GATEWAY (plus the package-fetch residue of UPDATER-BACKUP-NO-FAILOVER), UPDATER-INSTALL-REPREP, UPDATER-DUAL-INSTALL, UPDATER-STALE-CHECK-DATA; bundles B/C/D of the same scout are separate changes and appear only in NonGoals. Scoped to the read-only current state of worktree green-upd1 (branch spec/updater-net-bounds, base 689df8aa); anchors re-verified in that tree on 2026-11-22.

Goals.R-1: Bounded check, both layers: every check of the signed feed carries an explicit deadline. The renderer passes CheckOptions.timeout to the plugin check() in installSignedUpdate (commands/index.js:1334); m016 passes UpdaterBuilder::timeout before check() in mt_updater_check (m016_updater.rs:76) via a named constant. Values, justified: the check deadline is 15 s per request — the responses are metadata-only JSON (a latest.json feed is well under 10 KB), the deadline is the plugin's per-request bound, and the two-endpoint failover makes the honest worst case ≈ 30 s for a full sweep, which the 24 h-throttled launch check tolerates and the manual command turns into bounded feedback; this also mirrors the zone's rollback connect deadline (10 s, m068_rollback.rs:125). A check that hits the deadline is a real rejection inside the plugin — it must never surface as a quiet "no updates": on the manual path the existing statusNote rendering keeps showing a warning (file.check-update, commands/index.js:1363-1372), and on the install path the rejection lands in the localized failure state of R-4. The launch check's silent-by-design corner-2 (offline/feed errors do not advance the 24 h clock, pinned by e2e since C-66) is deliberately preserved — the deadline changes how soon the silent path settles, not whether it is silent.
Goals.R-2: Bounded download: update.downloadAndInstall receives an explicit options timeout (commands/index.js:1340) from a named constant — 300 s, matching the zone's rollback fetch deadline (ROLLBACK_FETCH_DEADLINE_SECS, m068_rollback.rs:129) for the same artifact class on the same fleet's worst link: the plugin's timeout is the reqwest whole-request bound (connect + headers + body — there is no per-chunk idle option through the plugin API), so the value must cover the largest artifact (~31 MB Windows installer per the m068 comment; ~14 MB compressed macOS archive) at ≈ 1 Mbit/s without false-failing slow-but-progressing transfers; a smaller value would manufacture failures, an absent value is today's infinite wait. The plan re-measures the actual shipped artifact sizes before pinning the constant in a test (the m068 constants-pin precedent, rollback_deadline_and_window_constants_are_pinned, m068_rollback.rs:2921-2927). A download that exhausts the deadline ends in the same visible localized failure as R-1 — never a stuck "Updating…" toast, never a silent return.
Goals.R-3: One install at a time: installSignedUpdate gains a single-flight guard (a module-scope in-flight promise in commands/index.js — both entries converge there by construction). While an install is live, a subsequent invocation is an explicit refusal: it invokes nothing (no second mt_rollback_prepare, no second check, no second downloadAndInstall), surfaces the localized in-progress notice, and returns; the guard clears when the live attempt settles (success or failure), so a retry after a failed attempt works as today. The guard is the serialization point because both known entries (file.check-update and INSTALL_UPDATE) live in the main window's single renderer context; the plugin command itself is left untouched (no mutex inside tauri-plugin-updater — an external crate this change does not modify).
Goals.R-4: Localized honest failure states for the install flow (the C-SEARCH-ERROR-VISIBILITY voice): the flow's terminal failure — deadline exhausted, download interrupted, signature or install error — surfaces exactly one localized failure notice (new updater.* keys, title + body, ten locales per C-62), with the raw error string demoted to the console marker; this replaces the hardcoded English «Update failed» toast for the shared flow (commands/index.js:1349-1351), and the in-progress refusal of R-3 uses its own localized pair. Existing test pins that expect the English catch copy are superseded by the localized-failure pins in the same suites. Nothing about the C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES raw-error-stays-console rule is relaxed.
Goals.R-5: Idempotent prepare, bounded re-copy: mt_rollback_prepare becomes idempotent against an intact staging set. prepare_inner reuses the existing staging snapshot — performing no bundle copy — exactly when the staged set provably belongs to the currently running version: the staging manifest parses with the current schema, its previous_version equals the running version, the platform matches, and the recorded digests re-verify against the staged files (the same readback discipline prepare_inner already applies at :515-528). Any other state — torn staging, digest mismatch, foreign version — wipes and re-prepares exactly as today (fail-closed kept). This is the deliberate mirror of the live-set validity rule: RollbackManifest::validate rejects previous_version == running for the live set (m068_rollback.rs:288-290, the rollback-to-self guard) precisely because a staging set of the running version is what an update attempt holds — the reuse criterion is that mirrored case, and it must not route through load_valid_live. The test seam follows the module's root-override convention (load_valid_live_at, :362-367): a root-explicit prepare variant so tests drive reuse and re-copy on temp fixtures, never the developer's real data root. The macOS ~30 MB copy is the target of the saving; the Windows version-only staging gets the same uniform contract.
Goals.R-6: Fresh-data install toasts: user-visible version strings in installSignedUpdate derive from the flow's own fresh plugin re-check, never from the queued notice snapshot — the progress toast names update.version from the check result that actually drives the install; the up-to-date toast keeps naming the running version (status.currentVersion — the running version cannot change within a session, so it is not stale-prone; re-verified at plan time). The stale-prone field (status.latestVersion) no longer reaches any user-visible string; INSTALL_UPDATE's handoff shape is unchanged. Every command's data freshness is then explicit: file.check-update and the launch check already check fresh per invocation; the install flow re-checks fresh; nothing derives a claim from a previous check's data.
Goals.R-7: Backup-channel honesty, no feed redesign: the feed-level failover is plugin-internal (2.14.1 src/updater.rs:545-658) and stays untouched; this change pins, with zero external network, that the backup channel delivers the package itself: a controlled local fixture (a failing primary endpoint and a mirror endpoint serving a latest.json whose platform url points at a local gateway-imitating route that serves the archive bytes) driven through the plugin's own injectable UpdaterBuilder seams (endpoint override + timeout, the pattern of the plugin's own tests) asserts that the package bytes are fetched via the feed-carried URL under the builder deadline — the Wave-4 criterion "for the backup channel, verify obtaining the package itself", discharged exactly as far as the architecture allows. Mark's code passing no URL anywhere and rewriting nothing is pinned on the renderer side: the flow hands only {timeout} options to check()/downloadAndInstall(), and the feed's URL is used as-is. The gateway-only package URL — and therefore the unavailability of a package fallback when the gateway is down — stays the recorded owner decision of C-UPDATER-STATS; this change neither adds a client-side GitHub fallback nor relitigates the counting design.
Goals.R-8: Governance: the touched governed files get VERSION bumps and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries per the modification checklist; the new renderer locale keys land in all ten locale files gated by the locale-keys test (tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js — the rollback.* namespace precedent, static/locales/en.json:1771-1779); the graph and verification deltas (M-016, M-068, V-M-016, V-M-068) land in the same bundle as the code with scenarios naming the new tests; app-store builds keep no updater surface (the m016 app-store stub and the isUpdatable gating are untouched); no version change, release, tag or publication is authorized by this specification.

Fix direction is binding: deadlines travel through the plugin's own timeout seams (JS CheckOptions.timeout / downloadAndInstall options / Rust UpdaterBuilder::timeout) — no timer races around the plugin calls, no reimplementation of download, no new dependency, no plugin source modification; the single-flight guard lives in installSignedUpdate (the shared entry), not in the stores; the prepare reuse lives in prepare_inner with the manifest-anchored criterion of R-5, not in the renderer.

Fail-closed ordering is binding and unchanged: mt_rollback_prepare strictly precedes check/download (the invocationCallOrder pins of C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK stay green); a prepare failure still cancels the update with no download; promotion of a fresh snapshot still happens only at boot reconciliation (main.rs:345-351); the reuse path may never promote, mutate the live set, or widen what counts as a restorable state beyond R-5's criterion.

Honesty bar: a deadline exhaustion is a real, visible failure state — nothing converts it into «is up to date», hides it, or silently advances the 24 h clock; the localized failure notice carries no raw error text in the GUI (console-only, C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES voice); new user-facing strings are localized in all ten locales; the pre-existing English strings that this change does not touch (the manual statusNote rendering, the Rust-side English convention) stay as they are.

Existing gates stay green and unweakened: the C-66 e2e matrix (update-notice.spec.ts) keeps its body — offline silence without clock advance, throttle, skip, deferral, store gate; the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK pins (prepare-before-check order, prepare-failure cancels, rollback confirmation semantics) keep their meaning; the m068 deadline/accounting suites are untouched; npm test, cargo test, e2e and grace lint stay clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline; app-store builds keep no updater surface.

No release or train admission follows from this specification; approval does not approve an unwritten plan; the draft enters through the standard review gates (two consecutive clean four-corner passes recorded before owner approval is requested).

NonGoals.NonGoal: A client-side package fallback URL (direct GitHub asset fetch when the gateway is down) for the forward updater: DownloadOptions has no alternative-URL field, the trust anchor is the minisignature rather than the URL, and re-deriving GitHub asset URLs in the renderer would duplicate m068's restore derivation and break C-UPDATER-STATS counting — that is an owner decision, recorded as such, not taken here.

Any redesign of the feed or the gateway: endpoints, /feed and /pkg routes, redirect semantics, counting, privacy surface and release.yml composition are untouched; the plugin's endpoint failover loop is consumed as-is and pinned, not reimplemented.

Modifying tauri-plugin-updater or @tauri-apps/plugin-updater, adding a plugin-level install mutex, or wrapping downloadAndInstall in Mark-owned transport machinery; the version pin (^2.14.1) and its resolution stay untouched (no Cargo.lock exists in the tree; plan re-verifies the resolved version's API shape).

The launch check's silence redesign (corner-2): offline/feed-failed automatic checks remain silent, do not advance lastUpdateCheckAt and raise no notice — the deadline only bounds how soon that path settles; making the auto path loud is a separate product decision.

Localizing pre-existing hardcoded English toasts beyond the flow failure states of R-4 (the «Update cancelled» prepare notice, the manual path's English statusNote rendering, the m016 Rust-side strings keep today's convention), download progress UI (F-UPDATER-PROGRESS-UI), staged rollouts, version_comparator, delta updates, and any rollback restore-path change (M-068's restore/CLI/pending machinery is read-only for this change except prepare_inner).
Bundles B/C/D of the same scout (PREFS-WRITE-TRUTH, RECENTS-SERIALIZE, SESSION-DURABILITY) and the m005/m017 surfaces; the Wave-4 keys 7-19 belong to those changes.
Creating plan.xml in this pass; implementing any R-item; touching .grace/graph or .grace/verification in this spec-only pass.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Bounded check (failing-first): before the fix, the renderer check call receives no options and the m016 builder carries no timeout; after, installSignedUpdate calls check({timeout}) and mt_updater_check's builder chain carries the named constant, both pinned by named tests that fail on the pre-change tree and pass after; the constants are pinned in tests (the m068 constants-pin precedent) and a hung check settles as a real rejection — the manual path still shows its warning, the auto path still stays silent without advancing the 24 h clock, and nothing anywhere renders a timeout as «is up to date».

Bounded download (failing-first): downloadAndInstall is called with an explicit {timeout} pinned by test; a download fixture that exceeds the deadline ends the flow in the localized failure notice with the raw error console-only, no relaunch, and the rollback set untouched; the constant's value is justified against measured artifact sizes recorded by the plan.

Single-flight (failing-first): two overlapping installSignedUpdate invocations produce exactly one prepare, one check, one downloadAndInstall; the second call settles immediately into the localized in-progress refusal and invokes nothing; after the live attempt settles, a fresh invocation runs normally (retry-after-failure preserved); the prepare-before-check ordering pin stays green.

Idempotent prepare (failing-first): with an intact staging set of the running version (manifest current-schema, previous_version == running, digests re-verified), a repeated prepare performs no bundle copy and keeps the set byte-identical; with torn staging, a foreign version or a digest mismatch it wipes and re-prepares exactly as today; both behaviors are pinned on temp fixtures through the root-explicit seam, and the live-set validation rules (including the rollback-to-self rejection at m068_rollback.rs:288-290) are unchanged.

Fresh toasts (failing-first): when the fresh re-check returns a version different from the queued snapshot's, the progress toast names the fresh version; no user-visible string contains status.latestVersion; the up-to-date branch still names the running version; the e2e shim (feed answer re-read per call) demonstrates the queued-notice-then-feed-moved scenario end to end.

Localized failure states: the shared flow's terminal failure surfaces exactly one localized notice from the new updater.* keys present in all ten locales and gated by the locale-keys test; the raw error appears only in the console marker; the in-progress refusal uses its own localized pair; superseded English-toast pins are updated in the same suites without weakening their settle-and-no-relaunch assertions.

Backup-channel evidence (Wave-4): a controlled local two-endpoint fixture — failing primary, mirror latest.json, gateway-imitating package route serving the bytes — drives the real plugin check/download through the injectable UpdaterBuilder seams with the deadline set, and the evidence records the package bytes arriving via the feed-carried URL under that deadline with zero external network; the renderer pins that no URL is constructed, rewritten or overridden anywhere in the flow; the two-endpoint Rust stand is mandatory for this criterion; a stand-in downgrade (JS timeout pins, URL-as-is pins, and the installed-plugin source citation for the failover loop) is admissible only under an explicitly named, individually justified seam failure recorded in the verification scenario as a named gap — never as a silent or blanket fallback.

Governance: VERSION bumps and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries on the touched governed files; M-016/M-068 graph deltas and V-M-016/V-M-068 scenarios land in the implementation bundle naming the new tests; ten-locale coverage passes; npm test, cargo test, the e2e suite and grace lint (--change C-UPDATER-NET-BOUNDS target during implementation, final --run-commands before handoff) are clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline; app-store stub suites stay green and the store build still exposes no updater surface.
